name: Kinim — Mixed Bird Offerings (Laws of Mixed-Up Pairs)
notes: Laws governing what happens when bird pairs (hatat and olah) become mixed up with each other or with other bird offerings, including rules of invalidation and valid remainder

name: Bird Hatat (Chatat haOf)
notes: Specific laws of the bird sin-offering, performed below the red line on the altar, distinct from beast chatat

name: Bird Olah (Olat haOf)
notes: Specific laws of the bird burnt-offering, performed above the red line on the altar, distinct from beast olah

name: Red Line of the Altar (Chut haSikra)
notes: The red line dividing the upper and lower halves of the outer altar, which determines where bird and beast offerings are performed

name: Obligatory Bird Offerings (Kinnim Chovat)
notes: Bird pairs brought as obligatory offerings (e.g., for birth, zivah), consisting of one hatat and one olah

name: Voluntary Bird Offerings (Kinnim Nedavah)
notes: Bird pairs brought as freewill or vow offerings, all of which are olot; no hatat is included

name: Assigned and Unassigned Bird Pairs (Mefurashin v'she'Einan Mefurashin)
notes: Distinction between bird pairs that have been assigned to specific purposes (hatat or olah) and those that have not yet been designated

name: Bird Flying Away and Invalidating Offerings
notes: Rules governing when a bird from a pair flies away into other groups of birds, the consequent invalidation, and calculation of which offerings remain valid

name: Pairing of Turtledoves and Pigeons
notes: Rule that turtledoves and pigeons cannot be paired together for a single kin; the hatat and olah must be of the same species

name: Leaving Invalid Birds to Die (Yumtu)
notes: Halakhic ruling that certain mixed or invalid bird offerings must be left to die rather than offered or redeemed

name: Priestly Discretion in Offering Kinnim
notes: Laws concerning whether the priest seeks guidance before offering mixed bird pairs, and the different outcomes depending on whether advice was sought

name: Women's Obligations for Kinnim
notes: Specific scenarios involving women who owe bird offerings for birth or zivah and the rules when multiple women's pairs become mixed

name: Conditional Vow Contingent on Birth
notes: A vow made contingent on giving birth, e.g., 'I vow a pair of birds if I give birth to a male child,' and the halakhic obligations that result

name: Torah Scholars' Wisdom Increasing with Age
hebrew: תלמידי חכמים כל זמן שמזקינין דעתן מתיישבת עליהן
notes: The principle that Torah scholars grow wiser with age, contrasted with unlearned people whose intellect diminishes; from the end of tractate Kinnim
